newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds dove on Tuesday, dragged down by weak Italian assets, with the bonos future contract ending 81 basis points lower at 113.98.
Dealers said 113.98 offered very strong support, making Wednesday's trend uncertain.
The peseta was also suffering from EMU jitters and ended around 84.73/77 per mark despite suspected massive intervention by the Bank of Spain around these levels.
The 10-year spread over Bunds briefly touched 130 bps before ending at 127 bps. Yesterday it closed at 115 bps. It has not traded at these levels since the end of November 1996.
A weaker peseta was adding pressure to the short-end of the yield curve. Dealers said views had changed from the morning.
Now they are expecting a rise in tomorrow's one-year bill auction rather than stable rates.
Latest grey-market yields were trading around 5.23/27 percent versus 5.15/19 percent as of this morning.
